video_title: Wemby ROUGH Finals Debut As Brunson, Knicks STEAL Game 1

quotes.speaker: Boogie Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson is the best closer in the NBA playoffs
quotes.excerpt: you know you have a real chance at winning a game with a Jalen Brunson on the floor
quotes.quote: In the playoffs right now, absolutely. I think he's proven that time and time again. Fourth quarter come around, you know you have a real chance at winning a game with a Jalen Brunson on the floor. I don't know what it is. It's like a flip switches, and if he started off rough, if he started off bad, that completely goes out the window. It's like a brand new game for him come fourth quarter.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's resilience and clutch performance against the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: the fact that he bounced back to stays with it and some of these shots he's hitting
quotes.quote: This kid's tough as nails. You never really see him leave the game like that, and so that was a little concerning for me. But the fact that he bounced back to stays with it and some of these shots he's hitting are unbelievable. They're so tough. By the way, he was riding Scott Foster last night. He was not stoked with Scott Foster's officiating. But just shout out to him for obviously, this game got a little bit out of reach there. I thought it was a wrap when they were down 13. Karl-Anthony Towns was great kind of getting them back in it. And then who better in the league right now than probably the most clutch player over the last four or five seasons in Jalen Brunson? Put the ball in his hands, let him work, get downhill, get to the basket, get to the free throw line, and hit just insane mid-range shots to will this team to a huge 10-0 lead so far and to steal one on the road is obviously very important in the finals.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's mastery of attacking specific spots on the floor
quotes.excerpt: he's a master of getting to his spots and everybody knows in the fourth quarter they're going
quotes.quote: I love the fact that he's so intentional with how he attacks. He's a master of getting to his spots and everybody knows in the fourth quarter they're going to put the ball in his hands, and it's nothing you can really do about it. As great of a defensive team that San Antonio is, last night they just got exposed. There were a lot of holes in their defense, and I felt like New York, they were able to get paint touches whenever they wanted, and I thought that was a dangerous game to play with New York, especially when you got a guy like Jalen Brunson that can get to his spots at will.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' resilience and collective effort in their Game 1 win
quotes.excerpt: the Knicks are a resilient team they are used to adversity they are never going to give up
quotes.quote: I think it's also just the Knicks are a resilient team. They are used to adversity. They are never going to give up to the last buzzer, and they have been in this situation multiple times. And even when when Brunson went down, Immanuel Quickley comes in, gives them good minutes. Karl-Anthony Towns gives them good minutes. Like this was a collective effort. At a certain point of the game, Josh Hart scored three points. He might have been the most impactful player on the on the game last night. Led the team in rebounds, assist, and steals while getting three points. Like that is the little OG hit huge. OG face-up Wembanyama like he wasn't even there in the corner. And just like this team is just rolling, they're playing confident, they're tough. They have a huge size advantage on the perimeter with this teams. They should pummel them on the glass. Like this is a tough matchup for the Spurs.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's defensive impact and the Knicks' response
quotes.excerpt: I thought it was Wembanyama's impact that made it feel like they were playing better defense
quotes.quote: I thought the Knicks did a did a great job of putting the Spurs' backs to the fire in that third quarter. They were up 14, Wembanyama goes out, and I said they're going to make a run when Wembanyama go out because I thought it was fool's gold. They were playing good defense, but I thought it was Wembanyama's impact that made it feel like they were playing better defense than than they were because New York was able to get into the paint whenever they wanted. But when they got to the paint, when they got there, Wembanyama was there and they were kicking out, driving, kicking out. But nonetheless, they were getting where they wanted to go. Wembanyama was just such a force at the rim, they couldn't get past him. Once they subbed him out of the game, that's when you saw the lanes start opening up and New York started being able to finish. Literally, the play that he went out of the game, they go down, straight to the rim and get fouled, get two free throws. And then you force Mitch Johnson's hand as a coach to put Wembanyama back in the game. Now he has to play extended minutes to the fact where I think he played I don't I don't know the exact number, but in the range of 15 to 17 straight minutes. He didn't have any opportunity to get him off the floor because that's how impactful he was on the defensive end.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns' crucial offensive rebounding and effort
quotes.excerpt: he was the person still on the offensive glass finishing two or three of those with and ones
quotes.quote: I got to I got to give Karl-Anthony Towns his credit because when it looked bad for the New York Knicks and everybody start tweeting and making their predictions that it was it was already over, he was the person still on the offensive glass, finishing two or three of those with and ones and keeping them in this basketball game. And every time it felt like this game was going to get out of control, Karl-Anthony Towns made a big play to keep them in striking distance for somebody else to be impactful after that. I don't I can't say that he was the best player on the floor, but he did his job, he did his part, and he was very impactful in that second half and keeping them close in this game and giving Jalen Brunson an opportunity to go out and close.

quotes.speaker: Boogie Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns' consistency and impact on the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: I do think he was one of the best players on the floor and it's been that way
quotes.quote: I think I can agree with Charles on that. I I do think he was one of the best players on the floor and it's been that way for the, you know, past couple of games as well, as far as just being consistent. Um, you know, even keel throughout this series. You know what you're getting for him every single night. Um, and he's giving them an opportunity to get to those fourth quarters where Jalen Brunson can then, you know, be the best version of himself.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns' physical and energetic performance
quotes.excerpt: he won the jump ball like literally like even from the tip this dude was dialed
quotes.quote: We talked about before the show, he won the jump ball like literally like even from the tip this dude was dialed. He was he had energy. His defense on Wembanyama was phenomenal. Like he was physical, he was pushing him out. So like 18, 12 and 4 isn't the craziest stat line, but it's the way he did it. It's the way how and the impact that the impact he had. It's the way he just with ease, blew by the best defensive player of this generation, like just because he obviously has to be aware of the way he shoots the ball from the perimeter. So like this guy, he made it look easy going against Wembanyama.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Legler's perspective on calling his first NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: it really, honestly, done it so much to me, it's always going to get come down to the same thing
quotes.quote: I'm great. I'm just Listen, after what we experienced as a crew, broadcast crew with all the blowouts we had to watch through the last two rounds, we were just glad to look up at the start of the fourth quarter and we actually had a a game that was winnable either way. We haven't had many of those in the postseason, at least not our group. So I was just excited for that. We had meaningful possessions in the fourth quarter. Honestly, no, and I that's that's everybody was asking me that. My wife asked me that. I talked to her right before I went out to the court. She's like, are you nervous? I said, no. It really, honestly, done it so much to me, it's always going to get come down to the same thing. At the end of the day, you're watching a basketball game, and I've been doing it communicating what I'm watching for a long time, 25 years at this place and in this industry. So, no, honestly, for me, it felt like, hey, once you sit down and that ball goes in the air, it's the same as it is every night.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's fatigue and the Spurs' defensive struggles
quotes.excerpt: it's a valid talking point because we saw it right there and there's times sometimes even we can
quotes.quote: Listen, there's no doubt it's a valid talking point because we saw it right there and there's times sometimes even we can see things because we're sitting there that maybe the cameras aren't going to catch. He was winded and gassed. There were times that he was really having a hard time like catching his wind, but and so there is there's some of that was there. But for me, when it when I look at it from the Spurs' point of view, they did not get him to the spots that he likes to catch the basketball as often as he was in previous rounds, certainly as much as he did in the Western Conference Finals. And it's not like they're out there playing in a vacuum, so you've got to give the Knicks credit. They were physical with him. That's one of the best defensive games I've seen any big man play against Victor Wembanyama this year, what Karl-Anthony Towns did to him in this game. But I thought the initiation of their offense wasn't as good as it needs to be.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's unique playing style compared to other smaller guards
quotes.excerpt: He plays a grounded game that relies on footwork, strength, balance, IQ, and touch.
quotes.quote: I don't think it's an invalid point when you look at historically, smaller guards trying to do this, particularly as your leading shot taker and leading scorer. He's not really in that category to me because of the way that he plays. This is a guy that's not relying on blowing by you and trying to get to the rim and beat a shot blocker to the spot. He's not a guy that's going to have to take really difficult pull-up deep jumpers all over the floor. He plays a grounded game that relies on footwork, strength, balance, IQ, and touch. Those are the five things, and I think for a lot of smaller guards out there, you've got to have the strength and the physical profile that Jalen Brunson has. He's a guy that's got good mass, so he can hold his position and leverage even when guys are pressuring him. The way he goes about it with his patience and his footwork and getting to his spots is different than what we've seen out of guys his size historically.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's composure and leadership in high-pressure situations
quotes.excerpt: I literally have run out of adjectives to describe this guy in pressure situations.
quotes.quote: He can still be efficient when he needs to be, and I said it on the broadcast and I mean it, I literally have run out of adjectives to describe this guy in pressure situations. He just carries himself like he's so sure of what the result is going to be in the most pressure-packed situations, and man does that calm down a team and calm down a head coach and calm down your role players when your best player is operating in that space.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Dylan Harper's elite performance warrants more trust from Mitch Johnson
quotes.excerpt: Dylan Harper to me is not somebody you consider a rookie anymore. He's past that point.
quotes.quote: I do think it hurt him and I think that's something that Mitch Johnson is going to go back and look at and he probably has already came to that conclusion before he went to bed last night because Dylan Harper is not a normal rookie. I'm going to go with the guy that's a little bit more of a veteran player, you trust him a little bit more in situations because Dylan Harper to me is not somebody you consider a rookie anymore. He's past that point, and a lot of that has happened, he had a great year, but most of it is really happened right here in the postseason. The moments that he has had, his ability to play against elite defenses, get to his spots, really overwhelm you physically because that's what he does. I said it on the broadcast, this is one of the most powerful one-and-done guards we've seen come into the league ever. He just plays through contact, his shoulders, his forearms, he's not phased by what's in front of him, and now he's making deep shots at a higher rate. I think that was something that they needed to go to in the fourth quarter, continued to let him run because he can get into the paint when he wants to.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: De'Aaron Fox is struggling with injury during the postseason
quotes.excerpt: De'Aaron Fox right now is not himself and he told us, look, he said it is what it is.
quotes.quote: De'Aaron Fox right now is not himself and he told us, look, he said it is what it is. I'm not 100%, trying to do the best I can. Right now, it may be that you go to Dylan Harper if they're in that situation, and again, it would not be surprised if game two, that's one of the main adjustments that Mitch Johnson is going to make.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's MVP potential and future impact
quotes.excerpt: you make your case for the next year in the postseason and that's what he's doing right now
quotes.quote: What happens a lot of time is you make your case for the next year in the postseason, and that's what he's doing right now. So Shai's back-to-back, but with what Wembanyama has done and getting them through that series and winning a game seven on the road in the fashion that he did, um, he's made his case now going into next season that he wants to to basically make this league his. And I think the impact that he has on both ends, he's going to be the front runner going into the season. No matter how this plays out, whether they win this series or they don't win this series, I think Victor Wembanyama has established himself going into next season as clearly the front runner, you know, to get an MVP. And if he gets one that young, watch out.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: The intensity and intimidation of the 1997 Chicago Bulls
quotes.excerpt: he's the only player that I've ever seen that had an insatiable appetite to attack
quotes.quote: I've covered LeBron, obviously, his entire career, but when you're on the court you see it, and what that looks like, and I've said it to this day, he's the only player that I've ever seen that had an insatiable appetite to attack. At no point could you relax. The entire time, like I'll I'll give you an example. Some other Hall of Fame players like I guarded during that time. Let's take a Reggie Miller for example. Incredibly difficult to guard, chased this dude around, if you got there late, you got your feelings hurt coming off a screen, all that. But at some point, Reggie Miller was going to throw the ball into Rick Smith a few times, and you could like relax. Like okay, this is somebody else's problem now. Same thing with a guy like Clyde Drexler. You know, what a problem to guard a guy that big at that position. He's going to throw the ball to Hakeem and kind of camp out a little bit. That wasn't the case with Jordan. Like when you're operating in that triangle offense, like every single movement was designed in his mind to catch it and attack and set himself in position to attack with his next movement. So the relentlessness with which he played is something I'll never forget, and to me, it's like kind of separates him from everybody.
